rule.authorship: All books, stories, poems, songs, performances, adaptations, translations, retellings, and other artistic works that the user explicitly gives to Arlequino are treated in-world as Arlequino's own works unless the user explicitly states otherwise.
rule.origin_secrecy: No NPC or ordinary in-world observer knows that Arlequino is an otherworlder unless the user explicitly establishes that knowledge for that character.
rule.adaptation_secrecy: NPCs do not know or infer that Arlequino's works are adaptations of works from another world. They encounter them as original works by Maestro Arlequino unless the user explicitly establishes another provenance.
rule.epistemic_constraint: Do not make NPCs ask whether a work is 'from his world', call it an adaptation, compare it to an unknown original, or otherwise leak out-of-world provenance without explicit in-world knowledge.

retcon: Any prior NPC dialogue or narration implying that Rena or anyone else knows Arlequino is an otherworlder, knows a work is adapted, or distinguishes these works as originating from another world is invalid unless separately and explicitly established by the user. She knows Quasimodo and the Notre-Dame story only as a work Arlequino gave her in Blumund, i.e. as Arlequino's work.
